question.problem: From a deck that contains $26$ colored cards, Rick randomly draws $4$ red cards. What is the probability of this event,  given that the deck contained $6$ red cards in total?
question.worked_solution:
Let $A$ denote the event described in the question. Then

$$
\begin{aligned}P(A) & =\frac{n}{N},\end{aligned}
$$

where $N$ is the total number of ways to draw $4$ cards out of $26,$ and $n$ is the number of ways to draw exactly $4$ red cards.

Note that since the order of the draws does not matter, we use combinations.

First, we compute $N.$ The number of ways to draw $4$ cards from a total of $26$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}N={}_{26}{C}_{4} & =\frac{26!}{4!\cdot 22!}=14\,950.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute $n.$ There are $6$ red cards in the deck, so the number of ways to choose $4$ of those cards (out of $6$) is

$$
\begin{aligned}n={}_{6}{C}_{4}=\frac{6!}{4!\cdot 2!}=15.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, 

$$
\begin{aligned}P(A) & =\frac{n}{N}=\frac{15}{14\,950}=\frac{3}{2\,990}.\end{aligned}
$$
